html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation; AI: artificial intelligence; IAM: Identity and Access Management; KMS: Key Management Service; FM: foundation model; LLM: large language model; SDK: software development kit; RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback; ROUGE: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation; BLEU: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy; A2I: Augmented AI; PII: personally identifiable information

  • See the whole exam on one page: domains, weights and where each topic lives
  • Tell look-alike ideas and services apart in pairs and sets
  • Use a need-to-service chooser for the questions that describe a need
  • Recall the lists the exam likes, and the terms that trip people up

2A one-page review of the whole course

Running case

Cedar and Salt's Final Review

  • Cedar and Salt's assistant now has models, prompts, your own data, evaluation, safeguards and an audit trail
  • Before the exam, you want one page per topic, not fourteen modules
  • Some look-alikes keep getting mixed up: RAG and fine-tuning, Clarify and Guardrails, Config and CloudTrail
  • Your job: review quickly, and fix the confusions that cost points

The Exam on One Page

Domain and weight Modules Core ideas
Fundamentals of AI and ML (20%) 1 to 3 AI, ML, deep learning; use cases and AWS AI services; lifecycle, MLOps, metrics
Fundamentals of GenAI (24%) 4 to 6 Tokens, embeddings, agents; strengths and limits; Bedrock, SageMaker AI, AgentCore
Applications of Foundation Models (28%) 7 to 10 RAG, parameters, prompting, fine-tuning, evaluation
Responsible AI (14%) 11 and 12 Guardrails, bias, Model Cards, explainability
Security, Compliance, Governance (14%) 13 and 14 IAM, KMS, Macie, PrivateLink, Config, CloudTrail, Artifact
  • 65 questions, 90 minutes, 700 to pass on a scale of 100 to 1,000
Exam tip

Domains 1 to 3 carry 72 percent of the exam; the three smaller domains are still worth the points.

Look-Alikes: AI and ML Concepts

Look-alikes Tell them apart
AI, ML, deep learning, GenAI, agentic AI Umbrella; learns from data; neural networks; creates content; acts toward goals
Supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement Labeled; unlabeled patterns; rewards
Classification, regression, clustering Categories; numbers; groups
Training, inference Build the model; use the model
Real-time, serverless, asynchronous, batch Instant; on demand; large or slow jobs; many at once
Underfitting, overfitting High bias; high variance
FM, LLM, diffusion, multi-modal General base; text; images from noise; several data types
Exam tip

Say the one-line job of each term before you look at the options.

Look-Alikes: AWS AI Services

Look-alikes Tell them apart
Transcribe, Polly, Translate Speech to text; text to speech; language to language
Comprehend, Textract Meaning in text; text and fields from scanned documents
Rekognition, Lex, Personalize Images and video; chatbots; recommendations
Amazon SageMaker AI Build, train and deploy your own models
Amazon Bedrock Foundation models through one API
SageMaker JumpStart Pre-trained and open models to deploy and tune
Autopilot, Glue DataBrew, Model Monitor Auto-built models; no-code data cleaning; drift checks
Exam tip

Pre-built AI services do one task; SageMaker AI is for your own models.

Look-Alikes: GenAI Platforms and Tools

Look-alikes Tell them apart
Bedrock, SageMaker AI Least effort, many providers; most control
Knowledge Bases, Guardrails, Prompt Management Managed RAG; filters; versioned prompts
Strands Agents, AgentCore An SDK to code agents; a service to run and govern them
Agents Classic The earlier Bedrock Agents service, closed to new sign-ups
Amazon Nova Amazon's own foundation models
Quick, Kiro, AWS Transform Work insights; AI development environment; code modernization
Provisioned Throughput, batch, on-demand Reserved capacity; discounted jobs; pay per token
Exam tip

Models through an API: Bedrock. Run agents: AgentCore. Managed RAG: Knowledge Bases.

Look-Alikes: Customizing and Evaluating Models

Look-alikes Tell them apart
RAG, fine-tuning, continued pre-training Your documents at question time; labeled pairs; unlabeled domain text
Distillation, RLHF, transfer learning Large teacher to small student; human rankings; reuse for a related task
Zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought No examples; examples; steps
ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore Recall overlap; precision overlap; meaning
LLM-as-a-judge, human evaluation Fast scoring with reasons; subjective quality
Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 Right overall; few false alarms; few misses; the balance
Exam tip

Look at the data first: labeled, unlabeled, teacher output or human ranking.

Look-Alikes: Responsible AI, Security and Governance

Look-alikes Tell them apart
Guardrails, Clarify, Model Cards Filters content; finds bias and explains; documents a model
Amazon A2I, Model Evaluation Human review of predictions; scores of model quality
KMS, Secrets Manager, Macie Encryption keys; credentials; sensitive data in S3
PrivateLink, IAM Private network path; who may do what
AgentCore Identity, Policy Who the agent is; what it may do
Config, CloudTrail, Inspector What changed; who did it; vulnerabilities
Artifact, Trusted Advisor Compliance reports; best-practice checks
Exam tip

CloudTrail records who; Config records what changed; Inspector scans for flaws.

Service Chooser: Building AI Applications

I need to… Use
Turn speech into text Amazon Transcribe
Use a foundation model through an API Amazon Bedrock
Build and train my own ML model Amazon SageMaker AI
Answer from my own documents Knowledge Bases (RAG)
Store embeddings next to SQL data Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector
Link entities and vectors Neptune Analytics
Complete a multi-step task through APIs An agent, run on AgentCore
Save prompts, variants and versions Prompt Management
Exam tip

Name the verb in the need, then the service.

Service Chooser: Safe, Secure and Compliant

I need to… Use
Block harmful content and mask PII Bedrock Guardrails
Catch ungrounded answers A contextual grounding check
Detect bias in data and predictions SageMaker Clarify
Document a model's purpose and risk SageMaker Model Cards
Keep model traffic off the internet PrivateLink
Find personal data in S3 files Amazon Macie
Show auditors AWS's compliance reports AWS Artifact
Record who called which API AWS CloudTrail
Exam tip

If two answers fit, choose the one that grants less access or needs less setup.

Lists the Exam Likes

  • Inference types: real-time, serverless, asynchronous, batch
  • ML lifecycle: business goal, framing, data processing, model development, deployment, monitoring
  • FM lifecycle: data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, feedback
  • Customization, cheapest first: prompts, RAG, fine-tuning, distillation, pre-training
  • Responsible AI features: bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, veracity
  • Scoping Matrix scopes: consumer app, enterprise app, pre-trained, fine-tuned, self-trained
Exam tip

Lists are easy points: say each one aloud from memory.

Terms That Trip People Up

Term Meaning
Hallucination, nondeterminism A confident wrong answer; different answers to the same prompt
Temperature, Top K, Top P Randomness; a fixed number of candidates; a share of probability
Token, chunk, embedding A piece of text; a split piece of a document; a vector of meaning
Transparent, explainable How it was built; why it answered
Grounding, source citation Answers tied to sources; showing which sources
Precision, recall Few false alarms; few misses
Exam tip

When two terms look alike, say the one-line difference before you answer.

3Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
One page five domains, 65 questions, 90 minutes, 700 to pass
Look-alikes learn the one-line job of each idea and service; the exam describes the job
Chooser name the verb in the need, then the service
